<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Update the existing HELIX game with a more complex, research-inspired evolution system beginning at the cellular stage, stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and a DNA bank for saving creature genomes.

## Requirements
- Deliver a complete, playable game or apply changes to the existing game.
- Base the evolution system on real genome and molecular research.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions recorded.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game UI, state and genetics logic, creature rendering, styling, and package scripts.

### Active
- Implement evolution stages, stage-dependent creature details, and a DNA bank.
- Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the evolution stages, creature details, and DNA bank in the existing game.
2. Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.
3. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, creature dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, selection, and UI logic.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution logic.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature rendering and creature system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is an existing Three.js game.
- `src/genetics.js` currently defines a 10-gene animal-trait genome and evolution using selection, crossover, and mutation.
- No implementation changes have been made.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Update HELIX’s evolution system to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing creature genomes.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and keep it playable.
- Base evolution on real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing UI, genome and evolution logic, creature rendering, styling, and package scripts.

### Active
- Implement evolution stages, stage-dependent creature details, and genome saving/browsing.
- Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement evolution stages, creature details, and genome saving/browsing.
2. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
3. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, creature dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, selection, and UI logic.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution logic.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature rendering and creature system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is an existing Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- The initial population has six founders; the dossier shows fitness components and trait expression.
- No implementation changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Update HELIX’s evolution system to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing creature genomes.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and keep it playable.
- Base evolution on real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing UI, genome/evolution logic, creature rendering, styling, and build scripts.

### Active
- Implement the cellular starting stage, stage-dependent selected-creature details, and genome saving/browsing UI.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the requested evolution stages, selected-creature details, and DNA bank.
2. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
3. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, creature dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, selection, and UI logic.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution logic.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature rendering and creature system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- The initial population has six founders; the dossier currently shows fitness components and trait expression.
- No implementation changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Update HELIX’s evolution system to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing creature genomes.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and keep it playable.
- Base evolution on real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game UI, state and evolution logic, genome model, creature renderer, and build scripts.

### Active
- Implement the cellular starting stage, selected-creature details that vary by stage, and genome saving/browsing UI.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the cellular starting stage, stage-dependent details, and genome bank UI.
2. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
3. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, creature dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, selection, evolution, and UI logic.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution logic.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature rendering and creature system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- The population currently starts with six founders; the dossier shows fitness components and trait expression.
- No implementation changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Update HELIX’s evolution system to start at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing creature genomes.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and keep it playable.
- Base evolution on real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game’s UI, state and evolution logic, genome model, creature renderer, and build scripts.

### Active
- Implement the cellular starting stage, stage-dependent details, and genome bank UI.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the cellular starting stage, stage-dependent details, and genome bank UI.
2. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
3. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, creature dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, selection, evolution, and UI logic.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution logic.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature rendering and creature system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- The population currently starts with six founders; the dossier shows fitness components and trait expression.
- No implementation changes have been made yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update HELIX’s evolution system to start at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing creature genomes.

## Requirements
- Keep the existing game playable.
- Ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game UI, state and evolution logic, genome model, creature renderer, and build scripts.

### Active
- Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
- Add a DNA bank UI for saving and browsing genomes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
2. Add the DNA bank UI for saving and browsing genomes.
3. Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, specimen dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, generation/evolution logic, selection, and UI rendering.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature renderer and population system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- Founders are created in `makeFounders()`; `advanceGeneration()` breeds and respawns the population; selected-creature dossier rendering is in `updateSelectionUI()`.
- Creature populations are rendered through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` in `src/creature.js`; the renderer builds animal bodies from gene values.
- The game currently starts at generation 1 with six founder genomes.
- No implementation changes have been made.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update HELIX’s evolution system to start at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing creature genomes.

## Requirements
- Keep the existing game playable.
- Ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions have been made yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game UI, state and evolution logic, genome model, creature renderer, and build scripts.

### Active
- Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
- Add a DNA bank UI for saving and browsing genomes.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
2. Add the DNA bank UI for saving and browsing genomes.
3. Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, specimen dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, generation/evolution logic, selection, and UI rendering.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature renderer and population system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- Founders are created in `makeFounders()`; `advanceGeneration()` breeds and respawns the population; selected-creature dossier rendering is in `updateSelectionUI()`.
- Creature populations are rendered through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` in `src/creature.js`; the renderer builds animal bodies from gene values.
- The game currently starts at generation 1 with six founder genomes.
- No implementation changes have been made.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Keep the existing game playable and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game UI, state and evolution logic, genome model, creature renderer, and build scripts.

### Active
- Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
- Add a DNA bank UI for saving and browsing genomes.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
2. Add the DNA bank UI for saving and browsing genomes.
3. Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, specimen dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, generation/evolution logic, selection, and UI rendering.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature renderer and population system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- Founders are created in `makeFounders()`; `advanceGeneration()` breeds and respawns the population; selected-creature dossier rendering is in `updateSelectionUI()`.
- Creature populations are rendered through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` in `src/creature.js`.
- The game currently starts at generation 1 with six founder genomes.
- No implementation changes have been made.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Keep the existing game playable and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the game UI, state and evolution logic, genome model, creature renderer, and build scripts.

### Active
- Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
- Add a DNA bank UI for saving and browsing genomes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
2. Add a DNA bank UI for saving and browsing genomes.
3. Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI shell, specimen dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, generation/evolution logic, selection, and UI rendering; `makeFounders()` creates the starting population, and `updateSelectionUI()` renders the dossier.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature renderer and population system; `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` creates the population.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- The game currently starts at generation 1 with six founder genomes.
- No implementation changes have been made.

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Keep the existing game playable and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected initialization/reset, evolution, genome logic, creature construction, dossier UI, layout styles, and event handlers.

### Active
- Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
- Add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage starting conditions and stage-dependent creature details.
2. Add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
3. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI shell, specimen dossier, controls, and help modal.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, initialization/reset, `makeFounders()`, and `updateSelectionUI()`.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature renderer and population system.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling and responsive layouts.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- Initialization, reset, and generation advancement are in `src/main.js` (`initialize()`, `resetStudy()`, `advanceGeneration()`); creature spawning is handled by `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()`.
- `updateSelectionUI()` renders the selected creature dossier; `Creature.build()` currently constructs a quadruped-style model.
- No implementation changes have been made yet.

input.prompt: Explore how Creature builds its 3D geometry and how CSS positions panels/dock, focusing on feasible implementation for cellular-stage beginning and a DNA bank modal/panel. Identify exact useful functions, layout constraints, and no edits. Thoroughness medium.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e497a5850ffeKuyzbc9W5SZV3z" state="completed">
## Findings

- **Creature geometry is genome-driven.** In `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/creature.js`, `Creature.build()` (around lines 148–255) maps genome values to body proportions, materials, and component builders. Separate methods build the neck, tail, legs, armor, and accents. `Creature.update()` handles spawn scaling and locomotion.
- **The app currently starts with a population, not a cellular-stage scene.** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js` creates founders and calls `creatures.spawnPopulation()` during `initialize()` (around lines 854–875). `resetStudy()` also rebuilds the population (around lines 612–635). A cellular opening would need to account for both paths—for example, by delaying or gating population spawning until the opening sequence ends.
- **The existing layout has clear desktop and mobile patterns.** In `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`, desktop panels are absolutely positioned, about 310px wide, and scroll within a viewport-bounded height. The ecology and specimen panels sit on opposite sides, with the dock centered at the bottom. At widths up to 900px, panels become bottom sheets above the dock; the lower log and chart panels are hidden.
- **A DNA bank can follow the existing modal pattern.** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` contains the field-guide modal markup. In `main.js`, `openHelp()`/`closeHelp()` manage its open state and accessibility attributes; backdrop clicks and Escape close it. The modal card is viewport-bounded and scrollable on mobile.
- **There is also an established mobile-sheet pattern.** The app uses `openSheet()`/`closeSheets()`, `.sheet-open`, and `#sheet-scrim`. The dock currently offers mobile buttons for specimen and ecology sheets.

## Implementation implications

A cellular-stage beginning is most naturally handled at the **startup and reset flow**, coordinating when the population is spawned, rather than only changing the creature geometry. A DNA bank can reuse the **modal/card structure and interaction behavior** of the field guide; if it is intended to remain a persistent, quick-access tool on mobile, the existing **sheet and dock patterns** are another fit.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Keep the existing game playable and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions have been made yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected initialization/reset, genome evaluation, creature construction, dossier UI, event handling, and responsive/modal patterns.
- No implementation changes have been made.

### Active
- Change startup and reset conditions to begin at the cellular stage.
- Add stage-dependent selected-creature details and DNA bank controls and actions.
- Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage starting conditions in `initialize()` and `resetStudy()`.
2. Add stage-dependent details in `updateSelectionUI()` and DNA bank UI/actions.
3. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI shell, specimen dossier, controls, and help modal; likely location for DNA bank UI.
- `src/main.js`: Initialization/reset, population and selection UI, and event handlers.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/creature.js`: Genome-driven creature construction and population spawning.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling and responsive layouts.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- HELIX is a Three.js game with a 10-gene animal-trait genome, population selection, crossover, and mutation.
- `initialize()` and `resetStudy()` currently start six animal founders; `Creature.build()` constructs quadruped-style models.
- `updateSelectionUI()` renders the selected creature dossier.
- Existing field-guide modal and mobile-sheet patterns can support DNA bank interactions.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Keep the existing game playable and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected initialization/reset, genome evaluation, creature construction, dossier UI, event handling, and responsive/modal patterns.
- Confirmed the game starts with six animal founders and uses a 10-gene trait genome; no implementation changes have been made.

### Active
- Change startup and reset conditions to begin at the cellular stage.
- Add stage-dependent selected-creature details in `updateSelectionUI()` and DNA bank UI/actions.
- Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage starting conditions in `initialize()` and `resetStudy()`.
2. Add stage-dependent details and DNA bank UI/actions.
3. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI shell, specimen dossier, controls, and likely location for DNA bank UI.
- `src/main.js`: Initialization/reset, population and selection UI, and event handlers.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/creature.js`: Genome-driven creature construction and population spawning.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling and responsive layouts.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- `initialize()` and `resetStudy()` currently call `makeFounders()` and spawn the six founders at `SPAWN_POSITIONS`.
- `updateSelectionUI()` renders the selected creature dossier.
- Existing field-guide modal and mobile-sheet patterns may support DNA bank interactions.
- Cellular implementation must work with existing creature construction, which currently builds animal forms from genome traits.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Keep the existing game playable and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions made yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected initialization/reset, genome evaluation, creature construction, dossier UI, event handling, and responsive/modal patterns.

### Active
- Change startup and reset conditions to begin at the cellular stage.
- Add stage-dependent selected-creature details and DNA bank UI/actions.
- Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage starting conditions in `initialize()` and `resetStudy()`.
2. Add stage-dependent details and DNA bank UI/actions.
3. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI shell, specimen dossier, controls, and likely location for DNA bank UI.
- `src/main.js`: Initialization/reset, population and selection UI, and event handlers.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, traits, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/creature.js`: Genome-driven creature construction and population spawning.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling and responsive layouts.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- `initialize()` and `resetStudy()` currently call `makeFounders()` and spawn six founders at `SPAWN_POSITIONS`.
- `updateSelectionUI()` renders the selected creature dossier.
- `Creature.build()` constructs animal forms from genome traits; cellular-stage representation needs to account for this.
- `advanceGeneration()` uses `breedPopulation()` and rebuilds the population as creatures; changes should preserve evolution and DNA-banking workflows.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-dependent details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Added DNA bank button markup to `index.html`.
- Inspected initialization/reset, generation advancement, specimen dossier, creature construction, event binding, styling, and build scripts.

### Active
- Set startup and reset conditions to begin at the cellular stage.
- Add stage-dependent specimen details and DNA bank storage, browsing, modal, and button behavior.
- Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-stage startup and reset in `initialize()` and `resetStudy()`.
2. Add stage-dependent selected-creature details and DNA bank interactions.
3. Build and run the game; verify functionality and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI shell; DNA bank button exists, but modal markup is not implemented.
- `src/main.js`: Initialization/reset, selected-creature dossier, state, and event handlers.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, population spawning, and movement.
- `src/genetics.js`: Ten-gene genome, evaluation, mutation, and population evolution.
- `src/style.css`: Game styling and existing modal styles.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- Startup and reset currently create six founders at `SPAWN_POSITIONS`; selected-creature details are rendered by `updateSelectionUI()`.

- `advanceGeneration()` uses `breedPopulation()` and rebuilds the population; preserve evolution and DNA-banking workflows.
- `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` expects positions for each organism, and `Creature.update()` animates animal movement.
- DNA bank button markup exists, but no storage, browsing, modal, or event handling is implemented.
- Changes are uncommitted; no build or visual verification has been run.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show details appropriate to the selected creature’s stage, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Cellular-stage organisms are represented as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a `stage` option to `Creature` and a `buildCell()` visual implementation in `src/creature.js`.

### Active
- Wire cellular stage into startup and reset while preserving later evolution.
- Make creature animation and the selected-specimen dossier stage-appropriate.
- Implement DNA bank storage, browsing, modal, and interactions; `index.html` already has a user-added `#btn-dna-bank`, but no bank modal markup.
- Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage while transitioning to later evolution appropriately.
2. Add a safe cellular update path in `Creature.update()`; existing movement and animation assumes animal body parts.
3. Update the specimen dossier with stage-appropriate details and labels.
4. Implement the DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Simulation startup/reset, evolution, specimen dossier, and event handlers.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, cellular representation, movement, animation, and population spawning.
- `index.html`: UI shell; includes the existing DNA bank button but no bank modal.
- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was already user-modified, and `src/creature.js` contains additional assistant edits.
- `buildCell()` is called when `this.stage === "cellular"`, but stage is not yet passed by population spawning or set at startup/reset.
- The cellular visual currently relies on shared body materials, while its `update()` path still proceeds into animal locomotion and body-part animation.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show details appropriate to the selected creature’s stage, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.

## Requirements
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and has a `buildCell()` visual implementation.
- Inspected current app structure and relevant source files.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning and replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add a cellular-safe animation/update path and transition to later evolution stages.
- Make selected-specimen dossier details appropriate to the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify functionality, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, and event handlers.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, cellular representation, animation, and population spawning/replacement.

- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and has a `buildCell()` visual implementation.
- Added the DNA bank header button (`#btn-dna-bank`) in `index.html`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning and replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.

6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was already user-modified, and `src/creature.js` contains prior assistant edits.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and has a `buildCell()` visual.
- `index.html` includes the DNA bank header button `#btn-dna-bank`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning/replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, event handlers, and state.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, cellular representation, animation, and population spawning/replacement.
- `index.html`: UI shell; includes `#btn-dna-bank`, but no bank modal markup yet.
- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was already user-modified, and `src/creature.js` contains prior assistant edits.
- `Creature.build()` selects `buildCell()` when `this.stage === "cellular"`, but stage is not passed by population spawning or set at startup/reset.
- `Creature.update()` currently animates animal body parts and needs a cellular-safe path.
- `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()` construct creatures without passing a stage.
- The dossier currently displays animal-centric details; stage-specific presentation remains to be implemented.
- DNA bank button exists, but `index.html` contains only help-modal markup.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and selects `buildCell()` for cellular organisms.
- `index.html` includes the DNA bank header button `#btn-dna-bank`.
- Added `this.cellGroup = cell` in `src/creature.js`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning/replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, event handlers, and state.

- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and selects `buildCell()` for cellular organisms.
- `buildCell()` stores `this.cellGroup`, `this.cellNucleus`, and `this.cellOrganelles`.
- `index.html` has the DNA bank header button `#btn-dna-bank`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning/replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, event handlers, and state.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, cellular representation, animation, and population spawning.
- `index.html`: UI shell; includes `#btn-dna-bank`, but no bank modal markup yet.
- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was already user-modified, and `src/creature.js` contains prior assistant edits.
- `Creature.build()` selects `buildCell()` when `this.stage === "cellular"`, but stage is not passed by population spawning or set at startup/reset.
- `Creature.update()` currently animates animal body parts and needs a cellular-safe path.
- `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()` construct creatures without passing a stage.
- The dossier currently displays animal-centric details; stage-specific presentation remains to be implemented.
- DNA bank button exists, but `index.html` contains only help-modal markup.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and selects `buildCell()` for cellular organisms.
- `buildCell()` stores `this.cellGroup`, `this.cellNucleus`, and `this.cellOrganelles`.
- `index.html` has the DNA bank header button `#btn-dna-bank`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning/replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, event handlers, and state.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, cellular representation, animation, and population spawning.
- `index.html`: UI shell; includes `#btn-dna-bank`, but no bank modal markup yet.
- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was already user-modified, and `src/creature.js` contains prior assistant edits.
- `Creature.build()` selects `buildCell()` when `this.stage === "cellular"`, but stage is not passed by population spawning or set at startup/reset.
- `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation(population, positions)` and `replace(index, organism)` construct creatures without passing a stage.
- `Creature.update(dt)` runs animal-specific movement and part animation; add a separate cellular animation path before those routines.
- `advanceGeneration()` respawns the population, while `resetStudy()` and `initialize()` also spawn it; all need cellular-stage initialization or stage propagation.
- The dossier currently displays animal-centric details; stage-specific presentation remains to be implemented.
- DNA bank button exists, but `index.html` contains only help-modal markup.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option, selects `buildCell()` for cellular organisms, and stores cell structure references.
- `index.html` has the DNA bank header button `#btn-dna-bank`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning/replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, event handlers, state, and DNA bank integration.

- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

- DNA bank button exists, but `index.html` contains only help-modal markup.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and selects `buildCell()` for cellular organisms; cell structure references are stored.
- `index.html` has the DNA bank header button `#btn-dna-bank`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning/replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, event handlers, state, and DNA bank integration.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, cellular representation, animation, and population spawning.
- `index.html`: UI shell; includes `#btn-dna-bank`, but no bank modal markup yet.
- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was already user-modified, and `src/creature.js` contains prior assistant edits.
- `Creature.build()` selects `buildCell()` when `this.stage === "cellular"`, but stage is not passed by population spawning or set at startup/reset.
- `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation(population, positions)` and `replace(index, organism)` construct creatures without passing a stage.
- `Creature.update(dt)` runs animal-specific movement and part animation; add a separate cellular animation path before those routines.
- `advanceGeneration()` respawns the population, while `resetStudy()` and `initialize()` also spawn it; all need cellular-stage initialization or stage propagation.
- The dossier currently displays animal-centric details; stage-specific presentation remains to be implemented.
- DNA bank button exists, but `index.html` contains only help-modal markup.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and selects `buildCell()` for cellular organisms.
- `index.html` has the DNA bank header button `#btn-dna-bank`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning/replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, event handlers, state, and DNA bank integration.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, cellular representation, animation, and population spawning.
- `index.html`: UI shell; includes `#btn-dna-bank`, but no bank modal markup yet.
- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was already user-modified, and `src/creature.js` contains prior assistant edits.
- `Creature.build()` selects `buildCell()` when `this.stage === "cellular"`, but stage is not passed by population spawning or set at startup/reset.
- `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation(population, positions)` and `replace(index, organism)` construct creatures without passing a stage.
- `Creature.update(dt)` runs animal-specific movement and part animation; add a separate cellular animation path before those routines.
- `advanceGeneration()` respawns the population, while `resetStudy()` and `initialize()` also spawn it; all need cellular-stage initialization or stage propagation.
- `updateSelectionUI()` currently displays animal-centric details; stage-specific presentation remains to be implemented.
- DNA bank button exists, but `index.html` contains only help-modal markup.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Update HELIX to begin at the cellular stage, show stage-appropriate details for the selected creature, and add a DNA bank for saving and browsing genomes.
- Preserve playability and ground evolution in real genome and molecular research.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them upon completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Represent cellular-stage organisms as cells with a membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Creature` accepts a `stage` option and selects `buildCell()` for cellular organisms.
- `index.html` has the DNA bank header button `#btn-dna-bank`.

### Active
- Pass stage through population spawning/replacement; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
- Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
- Update selected-specimen dossier details and labels for the current stage.
- Implement DNA bank modal, genome persistence/browsing, and interactions.
- Build and run the game, verify behavior, and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add stage state and pass it through `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation()` and `replace()`; initialize and reset in cellular stage.
2. Add cellular-safe animation and transition to later evolution stages.
3. Update dossier details and labels for the selected stage.
4. Implement DNA bank modal and event handlers.
5. Build, run, verify behavior, and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot (maximum width 1280px).
6. Summarize implementation choices and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Startup/reset, evolution, dossier rendering, event handlers, state, and DNA bank integration.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction, cellular representation, animation, and population spawning.
- `index.html`: UI shell; includes `#btn-dna-bank`, but no bank modal markup yet.
- `src/style.css`: Modal and application styling.
- `src/genetics.js`: Genome structure, mutation, and population evolution.
- `package.json`: Build and run scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was already user-modified, and `src/creature.js` contains prior assistant edits.
- `Creature.build()` selects `buildCell()` when `this.stage === "cellular"`, but stage is not passed by population spawning or set at startup/reset.
- `CreatureSystem.spawnPopulation(population, positions)` and `replace(index, organism)` construct creatures without passing a stage.
- `Creature.update(dt)` runs animal-specific movement and part animation; add a separate cellular animation path before those routines.
- `advanceGeneration()` respawns the population, while `resetStudy()` and `initialize()` also spawn it; all need cellular-stage initialization or stage propagation.
- `updateSelectionUI()` currently displays animal-centric details; stage-specific presentation remains to be implemented.
- DNA bank button exists, but `index.html` contains only help-modal markup.
